# 1. Field chronosequence and sand-matrix properties

## 1.1 Sand physicochemical properties

```{r sand-physicochemical-properties}
# Figure 1C
# 1) data input
df <- read.delim('~/Desktop/replot/metadata_nutrients/SD-SI.txt',
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
                 header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
df <- df[, 1:46]
df$Group <- as.character(df$Group)


# 2) Variable lists + Category

vars_physical   <- c("D50","Silt","Sand","Gravel","Ks")
vars_biological <- c("FVC","DNA")

meta_cols <- c("SampleID","SeqID","Group","Planted_years","When_planted","Kind","Type","Soil_size_mean")
vars_all <- setdiff(colnames(df), meta_cols)
vars_chemical <- setdiff(vars_all, c(vars_physical, vars_biological))

vars <- unique(c(vars_biological, vars_physical, vars_chemical))
vars <- vars[vars %in% colnames(df)]

var_category <- tibble(
  variable = vars,
  Category = case_when(
    variable %in% vars_biological ~ "Biological",
    variable %in% vars_physical   ~ "Physical",
    TRUE                          ~ "Chemical"
  )
) %>%
  mutate(Category = factor(Category, levels = c("Biological","Chemical","Physical")))


# 3) Long table + z-score (per variable across ALL samples)

dat_long <- df %>%
  select(Group, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(value = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))) %>%
  left_join(var_category, by = "variable") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(
    mu  = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sdv = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    z   = ifelse(is.na(sdv) | sdv == 0, NA_real_, (value - mu) / sdv)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# 4) GLM trend within SI (11–17): beta + p + adjR2 + BH
#    !!! use z for GLM (lm(z ~ Year)) to make beta comparable

si_years <- c("11","12","14","15","17")
min_total_n <- 12
min_years   <- 3

glm_res <- dat_long %>%
  filter(Group %in% si_years) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Group)) %>%
  group_by(Category, variable) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    d <- .x %>% filter(!is.na(z), !is.na(Year))   # <-- GLM on z
    n_eff  <- nrow(d)
    n_year <- n_distinct(d$Year)
    if (n_eff < min_total_n || n_year < min_years) {
      return(tibble(n = n_eff, n_year = n_year, beta = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, adj_r2 = NA_real_))
    }
    fit <- tryCatch(lm(z ~ Year, data = d), error = function(e) NULL)  # <-- GLM on z
    if (is.null(fit)) {
      return(tibble(n = n_eff, n_year = n_year, beta = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, adj_r2 = NA_real_))
    }
    sm <- summary(fit)
    beta  <- unname(coef(fit)["Year"])
    pval  <- sm$coefficients["Year","Pr(>|t|)"]
    ar2   <- unname(sm$adj.r.squared)
    tibble(n = n_eff, n_year = n_year, beta = beta, p = pval, adj_r2 = ar2)
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

glm_res <- glm_res %>%
  mutate(p_adj = NA_real_) %>%
  { idx <- which(!is.na(.$p)); .$p_adj[idx] <- p.adjust(.$p[idx], method = "BH"); . } %>%
  mutate(
    trend = case_when(
      !is.na(p_adj) & p_adj < 0.05 & beta > 0 ~ "Increasing",
      !is.na(p_adj) & p_adj < 0.05 & beta < 0 ~ "Decreasing",
      TRUE                                    ~ "NotSig"
    ),
    abs_beta = abs(replace_na(beta, 0))
  )


# 5) Ordering: Category then |beta| desc (NO inc/dec/ns grouping now)


trend_rank <- c("Increasing" = 1, "Decreasing" = 2, "NotSig" = 3)

order_tbl <- glm_res %>%
  mutate(trend_rank = trend_rank[trend]) %>%
  arrange(Category, trend_rank, desc(abs_beta), variable)

var_levels <- order_tbl %>% pull(variable)



# 6) Heatmap aggregation: median(z) per Group + Δ(17-SD)

group_levels <- c("SD","11","12","14","15","17")
min_n_per_group <- 3

agg <- dat_long %>%
  filter(Group %in% group_levels) %>%
  group_by(Category, variable, Group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_eff = sum(!is.na(z)),
    z_med = ifelse(n_eff >= min_n_per_group, median(z, na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Group = factor(Group, levels = group_levels))

agg_wide <- agg %>%
  select(Category, variable, Group, z_med) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Group, values_from = z_med)

agg_delta <- agg_wide %>%
  transmute(Category, variable, Group = "Δ(17-SD)", z_med = `17` - SD)

heat_df <- bind_rows(
  agg,
  agg_delta %>% mutate(Group = factor(Group, levels = c(group_levels, "Δ(17-SD)")))
) %>%
  mutate(
    Group    = factor(as.character(Group), levels = c(group_levels, "Δ(17-SD)")),
    variable = factor(variable, levels = var_levels),
    Category = factor(Category, levels = c("Biological","Chemical","Physical"))
  )


# 7) Wilcoxon SD vs SI17 (star on Δ cell) + BH

min_wilcox_n_each <- 5

wilcox_res <- dat_long %>%
  filter(Group %in% c("SD","17")) %>%
  mutate(G2 = factor(Group, levels = c("SD","17"))) %>%
  group_by(Category, variable) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    d <- .x %>% filter(!is.na(value))
    n_sd <- sum(d$G2 == "SD")
    n_17 <- sum(d$G2 == "17")
    if (n_sd < min_wilcox_n_each || n_17 < min_wilcox_n_each) {
      return(tibble(n_sd = n_sd, n_17 = n_17, p = NA_real_))
    }
    wt <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(value ~ G2, data = d, exact = FALSE))
    tibble(n_sd = n_sd, n_17 = n_17, p = wt$p.value)
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(p_adj = NA_real_) %>%
  { idx <- which(!is.na(.$p)); .$p_adj[idx] <- p.adjust(.$p[idx], method = "BH"); . } %>%
  mutate(star = ifelse(!is.na(p_adj) & p_adj < 0.05, "*", ""))

star_df <- wilcox_res %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = var_levels),
         Category = factor(Category, levels = c("Biological","Chemical","Physical"))) %>%
  filter(star == "*") %>%
  transmute(
    Category,
    variable,
    Group  = factor("Δ(17-SD)", levels = levels(heat_df$Group)),
    label  = star
  )


# 8) Row label coloring by GLM trend 

col_inc <- "#E3AF2E"
col_dec <- "#14A6B1"
col_ns  <- "#222222"

label_df <- glm_res %>%
  mutate(
    variable = factor(variable, levels = var_levels),
    lab_col = case_when(
      trend == "Increasing" ~ col_inc,
      trend == "Decreasing" ~ col_dec,
      TRUE                  ~ col_ns
    ),
    label = sprintf("<span style='color:%s'>%s</span>", lab_col, as.character(variable))
  ) %>%
  arrange(variable)

label_map <- setNames(label_df$label, as.character(label_df$variable))
missing_vars <- setdiff(levels(heat_df$variable), names(label_map))
if (length(missing_vars) > 0) {
  for (v in missing_vars) label_map[[v]] <- sprintf("<span style='color:%s'>%s</span>", col_ns, v)
}


# 9) Plot A: Heatmap

fill_pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#80cbc4", "#F3F6EC", "#ffa000"))(100)

p_heat <- ggplot(heat_df, aes(x = Group, y = variable, fill = z_med)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(
    data = star_df,
    aes(x = Group, y = variable, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4.2,
    vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  facet_grid(Category ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) label_map[x]) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = fill_pal,
    limits = c(-3, 3),
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Median z-score"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

p_heat


# 10) Plot B: Main Fig F (GLM bubble)
#     x = beta coefficient; size = adj R^2

f_df <- glm_res %>%
  mutate(
    variable = factor(variable, levels = var_levels),
    Category = factor(Category, levels = c("Biological","Chemical","Physical")),
    trend    = factor(trend, levels = c("Increasing","Decreasing","NotSig")),
   # adj_r2   = ifelse(is.na(adj_r2) | adj_r2 < 0, NA_real_, adj_r2)
  )

p_F <- ggplot(f_df, aes(x = beta, y = variable)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey30") +
  geom_point(aes(size = adj_r2, color = trend), alpha = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_grid(Category ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Increasing" = col_inc, "Decreasing" = col_dec, "NotSig" = col_ns),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    range = c(1.6, 8),
    name = expression("Adj. " * R^2)
  ) +
  labs(x = "SI trend (GLM beta coefficient)", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

p_F
```


## 1.2 D50 and hydraulic conductivity

```{r field-particle-size-D50-ks}
# Figure 1C
df <- read.delim('~/Desktop/replot/metadata_nutrients/SD-SI.txt',
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
                 header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
df_selected <- df %>%
  dplyr::select(Group, D50, Ks) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Group %in% c("SD", "17"))

group_colors <- c(
  "SD" = "#F4A64E",
  "17" = "#526F43"
)

common_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# D50

p_d50 <- ggplot(
  field_size,
  aes(x = Group, y = D50)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(fill = Group),
    width = 0.52,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    color = "#333333",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.70
  ) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(
    aes(color = Group),
    width = 0.16,
    size = 1.8,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  stat_compare_means(
    comparisons = list(c("SD", "17")),
    method = "wilcox.test",
    method.args = list(exact = FALSE),
    label = "p.signif",
    label.y.npc = 0.93,
    size = 5,
    tip.length = 0.02,
    bracket.size = 0.45
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.05, 0.18)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(D[50]~"("*mu*"m)")
  ) +
  common_theme +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 0, 5)
  )


# Ks


p_Ks <- ggplot(
  field_size,
  aes(x = Group, y = Ks)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(fill = Group),
    width = 0.52,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    color = "#333333",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.70
  ) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(
    aes(color = Group),
    width = 0.16,
    size = 1.8,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  stat_compare_means(
    comparisons = list(c("SD", "17")),
    method = "wilcox.test",
    method.args = list(exact = FALSE),
    label = "p.signif",
    label.y.npc = 0.93,
    size = 5,
    tip.length = 0.02,
    bracket.size = 0.45
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(

    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(
      K[s]~"(m"~day^{-1}*")"
    )
  ) +

# Combine

field_size_figure <- p_d50 /
  p_Ks +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1))

print(field_size_figure)
```

## 1.3 Mineral composition and PCA

```{r mineral-pca}
# Figure 1D
# Figure S1D–F

   # 1. Read data

    mydata <- read.delim(
      "~/Desktop/replot/culture/field-experiment/XRD/2020_field.txt",
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
      check.names = FALSE,
      header = TRUE,
      sep = "\t"
    )
    
    str(mydata)
    print(mydata)
    
   # 2. Basic data preparation

    
    # Ensure that the grouping variable is character
    mydata$year <- trimws(as.character(mydata$year))
    
    # Mineral variables:
    # all columns other than "year"
    mineral_cols <- setdiff(colnames(mydata), "year")
    
    # Convert mineral variables to numeric
    mydata[mineral_cols] <- lapply(
      mydata[mineral_cols],
      function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
    )
    
    # Check missing values
    if (anyNA(mydata[mineral_cols])) {
      stop(
        "Missing or non-numeric values were found in mineral columns. ",
        "Please check the input table."
      )
    }
    
    # Check negative values
    if (any(as.matrix(mydata[mineral_cols]) < 0)) {
      stop("Negative mineral abundance values were detected.")
    }
    
    # Add sample ID
    mydata$sample_id <- paste0("Sample_", seq_len(nrow(mydata)))
    
    # Numeric restoration age;
    # SD is deliberately coded as NA, not year 0
    mydata$restoration_age <- ifelse(
      mydata$year == "SD",
      NA_real_,
      as.numeric(mydata$year)
    )
    
    # Ordered display group
    group_levels <- c(
      "SD",
      sort(
        unique(mydata$year[mydata$year != "SD"])
      )
    )
    
    mydata$group <- factor(
      mydata$year,
      levels = group_levels
    )
    
    # Examine sums of mineral percentages
    mydata$mineral_sum <- rowSums(mydata[mineral_cols])
    
    print(
      mydata %>%
        select(sample_id, year, mineral_sum)
    )
    
    summary(mydata$mineral_sum)
    
    
 
    # 3. Closure to proportions
  
    # Even if the rows already sum to approximately 100,
    # close each sample to a constant sum of 1.
    
    mineral_matrix <- as.matrix(mydata[mineral_cols])
    
    mineral_prop <- mineral_matrix /
      rowSums(mineral_matrix)
    
    
    # 4. CLR transformation
    
    
    clr_transform <- function(x) {
      log(x) - mean(log(x))
    }
    
    mineral_clr <- t(
      apply(
        mineral_prop,
        1,
        clr_transform
      )
    )
    
    colnames(mineral_clr) <- mineral_cols
    rownames(mineral_clr) <- mydata$sample_id
    
    # Check CLR row sums; should be approximately zero
    print(rowSums(mineral_clr))
    
   
    # 5. PCA on CLR-transformed data
    
    # Do not scale again:
    # CLR values are already expressed on a common log-ratio scale.
    
    pca_fit <- prcomp(
      mineral_clr,
      center = TRUE,
      scale. = FALSE
    )
    
    pca_variance <- 100 *
      pca_fit$sdev^2 /
      sum(pca_fit$sdev^2)
    
    pc1_variance <- pca_variance[1]
    pc2_variance <- pca_variance[2]
    
    cat(
      "\nPC1 explained variance:",
      round(pc1_variance, 2),
      "%\n"
    )
    
    cat(
      "PC2 explained variance:",
      round(pc2_variance, 2),
      "%\n"
    )
    
    # PCA scores
    pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_fit$x[, 1:2])
    
    pca_scores$sample_id <- rownames(pca_scores)
    
    pca_scores <- pca_scores %>%
      left_join(
        mydata %>%
          select(
            sample_id,
            year,
            group,
            restoration_age
          ),
        by = "sample_id"
      )
    
    # PCA loadings
    pca_loadings <- as.data.frame(
      pca_fit$rotation[, 1:2]
    )
    
    pca_loadings$mineral <- rownames(pca_loadings)
    
    print(
      pca_loadings %>%
        arrange(desc(abs(PC1)))
    )
    
    
  
    # 6. Orient PC1 for interpretation
   
    # The sign of a PCA axis is mathematically arbitrary.
    # Here, PC1 is oriented so that increasing PC1 corresponds
    # to decreasing quartz contribution.
    #
    # Thus, positive PC1 generally represents a shift away from
    # quartz dominance and toward relatively greater contributions
    # from the other minerals.
    
    if ("Quartz" %in% pca_loadings$mineral) {
      
      quartz_loading <- pca_loadings$PC1[
        pca_loadings$mineral == "Quartz"
      ][1]
      
      if (quartz_loading > 0) {
        
        pca_scores$PC1 <- -pca_scores$PC1
        pca_loadings$PC1 <- -pca_loadings$PC1
        
        message(
          "PC1 direction was reversed so that higher PC1 ",
          "corresponds to lower relative quartz contribution."
        )
      }
    }
    
    
    
    # 7. Overall mineral-composition test
   
    # Euclidean distance on CLR data = Aitchison distance
    
    set.seed(123)
    
    permanova_result <- adonis2(
      mineral_clr ~ group,
      data = mydata,
      method = "euclidean",
      permutations = 9999
    )
    
    print(permanova_result)
    
    permanova_p <- permanova_result$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    permanova_r2 <- permanova_result$R2[1]
    
    
  
    # 8. Check multivariate dispersion
   
    # PERMANOVA can be influenced by unequal within-group dispersion.
    
    aitchison_distance <- dist(
      mineral_clr,
      method = "euclidean"
    )
    
    dispersion_fit <- betadisper(
      aitchison_distance,
      mydata$group
    )
    
    set.seed(123)
    
    dispersion_test <- permutest(
      dispersion_fit,
      permutations = 9999
    )
    
    print(dispersion_test)
    
    
 
    # 9. Restoration-age models
    
    # SD is excluded from these models because it is an unrestored
    # reference, not necessarily the actual year-zero state of the
    # restored sites.
    
    restored_scores <- pca_scores %>%
      filter(!is.na(restoration_age))
    
    # Linear model
    model_linear <- lm(
      PC1 ~ restoration_age,
      data = restored_scores
    )
    
    # Quadratic model
    model_quadratic <- lm(
      PC1 ~ restoration_age +
        I(restoration_age^2),
      data = restored_scores
    )
    
    summary(model_linear)
    summary(model_quadratic)
    
    anova(model_linear, model_quadratic)
    
    # Extract statistics
    linear_summary <- summary(model_linear)
    quadratic_summary <- summary(model_quadratic)
    
    linear_p <- coef(linear_summary)[
      "restoration_age",
      "Pr(>|t|)"
    ]
    
    linear_r2 <- linear_summary$adj.r.squared
    
    quadratic_p <- coef(quadratic_summary)[
      "I(restoration_age^2)",
      "Pr(>|t|)"
    ]
    
    quadratic_r2 <- quadratic_summary$adj.r.squared
    
    cat(
      "\nLinear trend P =",
      signif(linear_p, 4),
      "\n"
    )
    
    cat(
      "Linear adjusted R2 =",
      round(linear_r2, 3),
      "\n"
    )
    
    cat(
      "Quadratic term P =",
      signif(quadratic_p, 4),
      "\n"
    )
    
    cat(
      "Quadratic adjusted R2 =",
      round(quadratic_r2, 3),
      "\n"
    )
    
    
  
    # 10. Model-selection rule
   
    # Use the quadratic curve only if:
    # 1. the quadratic term is significant at P < 0.05, and
    # 2. adjusted R2 is improved relative to the linear model.
    #
    # Otherwise use the simpler linear trend.
    
    use_quadratic <- (
      !is.na(quadratic_p) &&
        quadratic_p < 0.05 &&
        quadratic_r2 > linear_r2
    )
    
    if (use_quadratic) {
      
      selected_model <- model_quadratic
      selected_model_name <- "Quadratic"
      
      trend_label <- paste0(
        "Restoration-age pattern: quadratic\n",
        "P", "\u209B\u2092", "\u00B2", " = ",
        format.pval(
          quadratic_p,
          digits = 2,
          eps = 0.001
        ),
        ", adj. R\u00B2 = ",
        sprintf("%.2f", quadratic_r2)
      )
      
    } else {
      
      selected_model <- model_linear
      selected_model_name <- "Linear"
      
      trend_label <- paste0(
        "Restoration-age trend: linear\n",
        "P = ",
        format.pval(
          linear_p,
          digits = 2,
          eps = 0.001
        ),
        ", adj. R\u00B2 = ",
        sprintf("%.2f", linear_r2)
      )
    }
    
    cat(
      "\nSelected display model:",
      selected_model_name,
      "\n"
    )
    
   
    # 11. Prediction data
   
    prediction_data <- data.frame(
      restoration_age = seq(
        min(restored_scores$restoration_age),
        max(restored_scores$restoration_age),
        length.out = 300
      )
    )
    
    prediction_values <- predict(
      selected_model,
      newdata = prediction_data,
      interval = "confidence",
      level = 0.95
    )
    
    prediction_data <- cbind(
      prediction_data,
      as.data.frame(prediction_values)
    )
    
    
    
    # 12. Group summaries
   
    pc1_summary <- pca_scores %>%
      group_by(group, year, restoration_age) %>%
      summarise(
        n = n(),
        mean_PC1 = mean(PC1),
        sd_PC1 = sd(PC1),
        se_PC1 = sd_PC1 / sqrt(n),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    
    print(pc1_summary)
    
    

    # 13. Plotting x coordinates
    
    # Put SD to the left with a clear visual gap.
    # SD is not treated as restoration year zero.
    
    minimum_restored_age <- min(
      restored_scores$restoration_age
    )
    
    sd_x_position <- minimum_restored_age - 2.2
    
    pca_scores$plot_x <- ifelse(
      pca_scores$year == "SD",
      sd_x_position,
      pca_scores$restoration_age
    )
    
    pc1_summary$plot_x <- ifelse(
      pc1_summary$year == "SD",
      sd_x_position,
      pc1_summary$restoration_age
    )
    
    
    
    # 14. Colours
    
    age_colours <- c(
      "SD" = "#E69F00",
      "11" = "#D9E878",
      "12" = "#B7CC63",
      "14" = "#8DAA55",
      "15" = "#718C47",
      "17" = "#4F6F3B"
    )
    
  
    # 15. Statistical annotation

    overall_label <- paste0(
      "Overall composition: ",
      "PERMANOVA ",
      "P",
      " = ",
      format.pval(
        permanova_p,
        digits = 2,
        eps = 0.001
      ),
      ", R\u00B2 = ",
      sprintf("%.2f", permanova_r2)
    )
    
    # Because plotmath and ordinary strings are awkward to combine,
    # use a clean plain-text label in the plot.
    overall_label_plain <- paste0(
      "Overall composition: PERMANOVA P ",
      ifelse(permanova_p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste0("= ", signif(permanova_p, 2))),
      ", R\u00B2 = ",
      sprintf("%.2f", permanova_r2)
    )
    
    
    # 16. Main one-panel figure

    set.seed(123)
    
    
    
    pc1_y_min <- min(
      c(
        pca_scores$PC1,
        prediction_data$lwr
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    
    pc1_y_max <- max(
      c(
        pca_scores$PC1,
        prediction_data$upr
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    
    pc1_y_range <- pc1_y_max - pc1_y_min
    
    # Add space for annotations
    plot_y_min <- pc1_y_min - 0.12 * pc1_y_range
    plot_y_max <- pc1_y_max + 0.23 * pc1_y_range
    
    
    set.seed(123)
    
    main_plot <- ggplot() +
      
      # Confidence interval for restoration-age model
      geom_ribbon(
        data = prediction_data,
        aes(
          x = restoration_age,
          ymin = lwr,
          ymax = upr
        ),
        fill = "#718C47",
        alpha = 0.15
      ) +
      
      # Linear fitted trajectory
      geom_line(
        data = prediction_data,
        aes(
          x = restoration_age,
          y = fit
        ),
        colour = "#3F5633",
        linewidth = 1.05
      ) +
      
      # Individual samples
      geom_point(
        data = pca_scores,
        aes(
          x = plot_x,
          y = PC1,
          fill = group
        ),
        shape = 21,
        size = 3.2,
        stroke = 0.55,
        colour = "black",
        alpha = 0.85,
        position = position_jitter(
          width = 0.08,
          height = 0,
          seed = 123
        )
      ) +
      
      # Mean ± SE
      geom_errorbar(
        data = pc1_summary,
        aes(
          x = plot_x,
          ymin = mean_PC1 - se_PC1,
          ymax = mean_PC1 + se_PC1
        ),
        width = 0.14,
        linewidth = 0.65,
        colour = "black"
      ) +
      
      # Group means
      geom_point(
        data = pc1_summary,
        aes(
          x = plot_x,
          y = mean_PC1
        ),
        shape = 23,
        size = 3.2,
        stroke = 0.75,
        fill = "white",
        colour = "black"
      ) +
      
      # Separate SD from the restored chronosequence
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = minimum_restored_age - 1.1,
        linetype = "dotted",
        linewidth = 0.55,
        colour = "grey55"
      ) +
      
      # Restoration-region label
      # annotate(
      #   "text",
      #   x = mean(range(restored_scores$restoration_age)),
      #   y = plot_y_max,
      #   label = "Restoration chronosequence",
      #   vjust = 1.15,
      #   size = 3.45,
      #   colour = "grey20"
      # ) +
      # 
      # Statistical annotation
      # annotate(
      #   "text",
      #   x = 11.05,
      #   y = plot_y_max - 0.055 * pc1_y_range,
      #   label = paste0(
      #     "PERMANOVA: P < 0.001, R\u00B2 = 0.60\n",
      #     "Age trend: P = 0.022, adj. R\u00B2 = 0.29"
      #   ),
      #   hjust = 0,
      #   vjust = 1,
      #   size = 3.15,
      #   lineheight = 1.15,
      #   colour = "black"
      # ) +
      
      # Positive-PC1 interpretation
      # annotate(
      #   "text",
      #   x = Inf,
      #   y = pc1_y_max,
      #   label = "Greater relative\nmicrocline contribution",
      #   hjust = 1.04,
      #   vjust = 1.05,
      #   size = 2.9,
      #   lineheight = 0.95,
      #   colour = "#3F5633"
      # ) +
      
      # Negative-PC1 interpretation
      # annotate(
      #   "text",
      #   x = Inf,
      #   y = pc1_y_min,
      #   # label = paste0(
      #   #   "Greater relative quartz, albite,\n",
      #   #   "and muscovite contributions"
      #   # ),
      #   hjust = 1.04,
      #   vjust = -0.10,
      #   size = 2.9,
      #   lineheight = 0.95,
      #   colour = "grey35"
      # ) +
      
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = age_colours,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = c(
          sd_x_position,
          sort(unique(restored_scores$restoration_age))
        ),
        labels = c(
          "SD",
          sort(unique(restored_scores$restoration_age))
        ),
        expand = expansion(
          mult = c(0.07, 0.08)
        )
      ) +
      
      scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(
          plot_y_min,
          plot_y_max
        ),
        expand = expansion(
          mult = c(0, 0)
        )
      ) +
      
      labs(
        x = "Restoration age (years)",
        y = paste0(
          "Mineral composition PC1 (",
          sprintf("%.1f", pc1_variance),
          "% variance)"
        )
      ) +
      
      theme_classic(
        base_size = 16
      ) +
      
      theme(
        axis.title = element_text(
          colour = "black",
          size = 16
        ),
        axis.text = element_text(
          colour = "black",
          size = 16
        ),
        axis.line = element_line(
          colour = "black",
          linewidth = 0.55
        ),
        axis.ticks = element_line(
          colour = "black",

        ),

        plot.margin = margin(

    print(main_plot)
    

    # figure s1D-F for XRD mineral composition
    #
    # A. CLR-PCA ordination, labeled as S1D
    # B. PC1 mineral loadings, labeled as S1E
    # C. Original mineral proportions across restoration stages, labeled as S1F
    # This code continues from the previous main-figure script.
    
    # 1. Prepare CLR data in long format

    
    clr_data <- as.data.frame(mineral_clr)
    
    clr_data$sample_id <- rownames(clr_data)
    
    clr_data <- clr_data %>%
      left_join(
        mydata %>%
          select(
            sample_id,
            year,
            group,
            restoration_age
          ),
        by = "sample_id"
      )
    
    clr_long <- clr_data %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = all_of(mineral_cols),
        names_to = "mineral",
        values_to = "clr_value"
      )
    
    clr_long$mineral <- factor(
      clr_long$mineral,
      levels = mineral_cols
    )
    
    
  
    # 2. Statistical analysis of individual minerals

    
    # For each mineral:
    # 1. overall difference among SD and all restored stages;
    # 2. linear restoration-age trend using only 11–17-year sites;
    # 3. BH correction across the five minerals.
    
    mineral_statistics <- clr_long %>%
      group_by(mineral) %>%
      group_modify(
        ~{
          
          mineral_all <- .x
          
          mineral_restored <- .x %>%
            filter(!is.na(restoration_age))
          
          # Overall group model
          overall_model <- lm(
            clr_value ~ group,
            data = mineral_all
          )
          
          overall_anova <- anova(overall_model)
          
          overall_p <- overall_anova[
            "group",
            "Pr(>F)"
          ]
          
          # Linear restoration-age model
          age_model <- lm(
            clr_value ~ restoration_age,
            data = mineral_restored
          )
          
          age_model_summary <- summary(age_model)
          
          age_p <- coef(age_model_summary)[
            "restoration_age",
            "Pr(>|t|)"
          ]
          
          age_beta <- coef(age_model_summary)[
            "restoration_age",
            "Estimate"
          ]
          
          age_adj_r2 <- age_model_summary$adj.r.squared
          
          # Quadratic model, reported for checking only
          quadratic_model <- lm(
            clr_value ~ restoration_age +
              I(restoration_age^2),
            data = mineral_restored
          )
          
          quadratic_summary <- summary(quadratic_model)
          
          quadratic_p <- coef(quadratic_summary)[
            "I(restoration_age^2)",
            "Pr(>|t|)"
          ]
          
          quadratic_adj_r2 <- quadratic_summary$adj.r.squared
          
          tibble(
            overall_p = overall_p,
            age_beta = age_beta,
            age_p = age_p,
            age_adj_r2 = age_adj_r2,
            quadratic_p = quadratic_p,
            quadratic_adj_r2 = quadratic_adj_r2
          )
        }
      ) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(
        overall_q = p.adjust(
          overall_p,
          method = "BH"
        ),
        age_q = p.adjust(
          age_p,
          method = "BH"
        ),
        quadratic_q = p.adjust(
          quadratic_p,
          method = "BH"
        ),
        trend_direction = case_when(
          age_beta > 0 ~ "Positive",
          age_beta < 0 ~ "Negative",
          TRUE ~ "None"
        )
      )
    
    print(mineral_statistics)
    
    
    # Save statistics
    write.table(
      mineral_statistics,
      file = file.path(
        output_directory,
        "XRD_individual_mineral_statistics.tsv"
      ),
      sep = "\t",
      quote = FALSE,
      row.names = FALSE
    )
    
    
    
    # 3. Panel A: CLR-PCA ordination
 
    # Group centroids
    pca_centroids <- pca_scores %>%
      group_by(
        group,
        year,
        restoration_age
      ) %>%
      summarise(
        PC1 = mean(PC1),
        PC2 = mean(PC2),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    
    # Temporal trajectory for restored sites only
    restored_centroids <- pca_centroids %>%
      filter(year != "SD") %>%
      arrange(restoration_age)
    
    
    panel_A <- ggplot(
      pca_scores,
      aes(
        x = PC1,
        y = PC2
      )
    ) +
      
      # Connect restored centroids chronologically
      geom_path(
        data = restored_centroids,
        aes(
          x = PC1,
          y = PC2,
          group = 1
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        colour = "grey35",
        linewidth = 0.7,
        arrow = arrow(
          length = unit(0.12, "cm"),
          type = "closed"
        )
      ) +
      
      # Individual samples
      geom_point(
        aes(
          fill = group
        ),
        shape = 21,
        size = 3.1,
        stroke = 0.55,
        colour = "black",
        alpha = 0.85
      ) +
      
      # Group centroids
      geom_point(
        data = pca_centroids,
        aes(
          x = PC1,
          y = PC2
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 23,
        size = 3.4,
        stroke = 0.75,
        fill = "white",
        colour = "black"
      ) +
      
      # Group labels
      geom_text_repel(
        data = pca_centroids,
        aes(
          x = PC1,
          y = PC2,
          label = year
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        size = 6.1,
        colour = "black",
        min.segment.length = 0,
        box.padding = 0.25,
        point.padding = 0.25,
        seed = 123,
        show.legend = FALSE
      ) +
      
     # Statistical result
      annotate(
        "text",
        x = Inf,
        y = -Inf,
        label = paste0(
          "PERMANOVA: P < 0.001, R\u00B2 = 0.60\n",
          "Dispersion: P = 0.293"
        ),
        hjust = 1.03,
        vjust = -0.35,
        size = 3.0,
        lineheight = 1.1
      ) +
      
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = age_colours,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      
      labs(
        x = paste0(
          "PC1 (",
          sprintf("%.1f", pc1_variance),
          "%)"
        ),
        y = paste0(
          "PC2 (",
          sprintf("%.1f", pc2_variance),
          "%)"
        )
      ) +
      
      coord_equal(
        clip = "off"
      ) +
      
      theme_classic(
        base_size = 16
      ) +
      
      theme(
        axis.title = element_text(
          size = 16,
          colour = "black"
        ),
        axis.text = element_text(
          size = 16,
          colour = "black"
        ),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.margin = margin(
          t = 10,
          r = 12,
          b = 10,
          l = 10
        )
      )
    panel_A
    
    
   
    # 4. Panel B: PC1 loadings
  
    
    loading_plot_data <- pca_loadings %>%
      select(
        mineral,
        PC1
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        mineral = factor(
          mineral,
          levels = mineral[
            order(PC1)
          ]
        ),
        loading_direction = ifelse(
          PC1 >= 0,
          "Positive",
          "Negative"
        ),
        loading_label = sprintf(
          "%+.2f",
          PC1
        )
      )
    
    
    panel_B <- ggplot(
      loading_plot_data,
      aes(
        x = PC1,
        y = mineral,
        fill = loading_direction
      )
    ) +
      
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        linewidth = 0.55,
        colour = "black"
      ) +
      
      geom_col(
        width = 0.66,
        colour = "black",
        linewidth = 0.35
      ) +
      
      geom_text(
        aes(
          label = loading_label,
          hjust = ifelse(
            PC1 >= 0,
            -0.12,
            1.12
          )
        ),
        size = 4.5,
        colour = "black"
      ) +
      
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "Positive" = "#718C47",
          "Negative" = "#B7B7B7"
        )
      ) +
      
      scale_x_continuous(
        limits = c(
          min(loading_plot_data$PC1) - 0.15,
          max(loading_plot_data$PC1) + 0.15
        ),
        breaks = seq(
          -0.6,
          0.8,
          by = 0.2
        ),
        expand = expansion(
          mult = c(0, 0)
        )
      ) +
      
      labs(
        x = "PC1 loading",
        y = NULL
      ) +
      
      theme_classic(
        base_size = 16
      ) +
      
      theme(
        axis.title = element_text(
          size = 16,
          colour = "black"
        ),
        axis.text.x = element_text(
          size = 16,
          colour = "black", angle = 25, hjust = 0.8,vjust = 0.8
        ),
        axis.text.y = element_text(
          size = 16,
          colour = "black"
        ),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.margin = margin(
          t = 7,
          r = 22,
          b = 8,
          l = 7
        )
      )
    panel_B
    
    
  
    # Panel C: Original mineral proportions
    #
    # Statistics:
    # 1. Kruskal–Wallis:
    #    SD + all restored stages as categorical groups
    #
    # 2. Linear regression:
    #    restoration age as a continuous variable;
    #    restored sites only (11–17 years)
    #
    # 3. BH correction:
    #    separately across the five minerals
    #
    # Plot:
    # - original mineral percentages
    # - individual samples
    # - mean ± SE
    # - linear trend and 95% confidence interval
 

   
    # 1. Basic variables
    
    # All mineral columns
    mineral_cols <- setdiff(
      colnames(mydata),
      c(
        "year",
        "sample_id",
        "restoration_age",
        "group",
        "mineral_sum"
      )
    )
    
    # Keep only numeric mineral columns
    mineral_cols <- mineral_cols[
      vapply(
        mydata[mineral_cols],
        is.numeric,
        logical(1)
      )
    ]
    
    print(mineral_cols)
    
    
    # Ensure year is character
    mydata$year <- trimws(
      as.character(mydata$year)
    )
    
    # Sample ID
    if (!"sample_id" %in% colnames(mydata)) {
      mydata$sample_id <- paste0(
        "Sample_",
        seq_len(nrow(mydata))
      )
    }
    
    # Restoration age:
    # SD is not coded as year zero
    mydata$restoration_age <- ifelse(
      mydata$year == "SD",
      NA_real_,
      as.numeric(mydata$year)
    )
    
    # Ordered group
    group_levels <- c(
      "SD",
      as.character(
        sort(
          unique(
            mydata$restoration_age[
              !is.na(mydata$restoration_age)
            ]
          )
        )
      )
    )
    
    mydata$group <- factor(
      mydata$year,
      levels = group_levels
    )
    
    
   
    # 2. Convert to long format
   
    
    mineral_raw_long <- mydata %>%
      select(
        sample_id,
        year,
        group,
        restoration_age,
        all_of(mineral_cols)
      ) %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = all_of(mineral_cols),
        names_to = "mineral",
        values_to = "percentage"
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        mineral = factor(
          mineral,
          levels = mineral_cols
        )
      )
    
    print(mineral_raw_long)
    
    
  
    # 3. Plotting positions

    
    minimum_restored_age <- min(
      mineral_raw_long$restoration_age,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    
    sd_x_position <- minimum_restored_age - 2.2
    
    divider_x_position <- minimum_restored_age - 1.1
    
    mineral_raw_long <- mineral_raw_long %>%
      mutate(
        plot_x = ifelse(
          year == "SD",
          sd_x_position,
          restoration_age
        )
      )
    
    

    # 4. Group summary:
    # mean ± SE
 
    
    mineral_raw_summary <- mineral_raw_long %>%
      group_by(
        mineral,
        group,
        year,
        restoration_age,
        plot_x
      ) %>%
      summarise(
        n = sum(!is.na(percentage)),
        mean_percentage = mean(
          percentage,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        sd_percentage = sd(
          percentage,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        se_percentage = sd_percentage / sqrt(n),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    
    print(mineral_raw_summary)
    
    
 
    # 5. Statistics
   
    # KW:
    #   all six stages
    #
    # Linear regression:
    #   restored sites only
    #
    # Both use original percentages.
    
    mineral_statistics <- mineral_raw_long %>%
      group_by(mineral) %>%
      group_modify(
        ~{
          
          current_all <- .x %>%
            filter(
              !is.na(percentage),
              !is.na(group)
            )
          
          current_restored <- .x %>%
            filter(
              !is.na(percentage),
              !is.na(restoration_age)
            )
          
          # Kruskal–Wallis test
          kw_result <- kruskal.test(
            percentage ~ group,
            data = current_all
          )
          
          # Linear regression
          linear_model <- lm(
            percentage ~ restoration_age,
            data = current_restored
          )
          
          linear_summary <- summary(
            linear_model
          )
          
          linear_beta <- coef(
            linear_summary
          )[
            "restoration_age",
            "Estimate"
          ]
          
          linear_p <- coef(
            linear_summary
          )[
            "restoration_age",
            "Pr(>|t|)"
          ]
          
          linear_adj_r2 <- linear_summary$adj.r.squared
          
          tibble(
            kw_p = kw_result$p.value,
            linear_beta = linear_beta,
            linear_p = linear_p,
            linear_adj_r2 = linear_adj_r2
          )
        }
      ) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(
        # BH adjustment across five minerals
        kw_q = p.adjust(
          kw_p,
          method = "BH"
        ),
        linear_q = p.adjust(
          linear_p,
          method = "BH"
        ),
        trend_direction = case_when(
          linear_beta > 0 ~ "Positive",
          linear_beta < 0 ~ "Negative",
          TRUE ~ "None"
        )
      )
    
    print(mineral_statistics)
    
 
    
  
    # 6. Statistical labels
 
    
    format_q_value <- function(x) {
      
      ifelse(
        x < 0.001,
        "q < 0.001",
        paste0(
          "q = ",
          sprintf("%.3f", x)
        )
      )
    }
    
    mineral_stat_labels <- mineral_statistics %>%
      mutate(
        label = paste0(
          "Kruskal\u2013Wallis: ",
          format_q_value(kw_q),
          "\n",
          "Linear regression: ",
          format_q_value(linear_q)
        )
      )
    
    print(mineral_stat_labels)
    
    
    
    # 7. Colours
   
    
    age_colours <- c(
      "SD" = "#E69F00",
      "11" = "#DDE879",
      "12" = "#BCCF67",
      "14" = "#91AA58",
      "15" = "#718C47",
      "17" = "#4F6F3B"
    )
    
    
  
    # 8. Panel C

    set.seed(123)
    
    
    mineral_order <- c(
      "Microcline",
      "Clinochlore",
      "Quartz",
      "Albite",
      "Muscovite"
    )
    
    mineral_raw_long$mineral <- factor(
      mineral_raw_long$mineral,
      levels = mineral_order
    )
    
    mineral_raw_summary$mineral <- factor(
      mineral_raw_summary$mineral,
      levels = mineral_order
    )
    
    mineral_stat_labels$mineral <- factor(
      mineral_stat_labels$mineral,
      levels = mineral_order
    )
    
    
    panel_C <- ggplot() +
      
      # Linear regression and 95% CI:
      # restored sites only
      geom_smooth(
        data = mineral_raw_long %>%
          filter(
            !is.na(restoration_age)
          ),
        aes(
          x = restoration_age,
          y = percentage
        ),
        method = "lm",
        formula = y ~ x,
        se = TRUE,

        inherit.aes = FALSE,

     # Statistical results
      geom_text(

        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        hjust = 1.03,
```

# 2. Microbial diversity and community succession

## 2.1 Beta-diversity

```{r beta-diversity}
# Figure 2A
# SD vs SI PCoA (Bray-Curtis)
# + SI year gradient + centroid trajectory
# + PERMANOVA + PERMDISP

# SD vs SI PCoA (Bray-Curtis)
# + SI year gradient
# + SD/SI ellipses
# + PERMANOVA (only)
# + prevalence filter: >=10% non-zero in SD+SI

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(vegan)
  library(stringr)
})

# 1) Load data 
infile <- "~/Desktop/replot/meta/species_all_acpm.txt"

df <- read.delim(
  infile,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE,
  row.names = 1,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t"
)

stopifnot(all(c("kind", "year") %in% colnames(df)))

# 2) Keep SD & SI only
target_years <- c("11", "12", "14", "15", "17")   

df_sub <- df %>%
  filter(kind %in% c("SD", "SI")) %>%
  mutate(
    kind = factor(kind, levels = c("SD", "SI")),
    year_chr = str_trim(as.character(year))
  ) %>%
  
 
  filter(kind == "SD" | (kind == "SI" & year_chr %in% target_years)) %>%
  mutate(
    year_chr = factor(year_chr, levels = target_years),
    #  ellipse 
    group2 = kind
  )

# 3) Build abundance matrix + prevalence filter 
meta_cols <- intersect(c("group", "kind", "year", "year_chr", "group2"), colnames(df_sub))
otu <- df_sub %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols))

otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu)
mode(otu_mat) <- "numeric"
otu_mat[is.na(otu_mat)] <- 0

# Remove all-zero species first (optional)
otu_mat <- otu_mat[, colSums(otu_mat) > 0, drop = FALSE]

# Prevalence filter: keep species present (non-zero) in >=10% samples (within SD+SI subset)
prev_cutoff <- 0.10
n_samples <- nrow(otu_mat)
min_n_nonzero <- ceiling(prev_cutoff * n_samples)

nonzero_counts <- colSums(otu_mat > 0)
keep_cols <- nonzero_counts >= min_n_nonzero
otu_mat <- otu_mat[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]

cat("Samples (SD+SI):", n_samples, "\n")
cat("Species kept (>=10% non-zero):", ncol(otu_mat), "\n")

# 4) Bray-Curtis distance 
dist_bc <- vegdist(otu_mat, method = "bray")

# 5) PCoA (cmdscale) 
pcoa <- cmdscale(dist_bc, k = 2, eig = TRUE)

coords <- as.data.frame(pcoa$points)
colnames(coords) <- c("Dim1", "Dim2")
coords$sample <- rownames(coords)

# variance explained (approx, using positive eigenvalues)
eig <- pcoa$eig
eig_pos <- eig[eig > 0]
var_exp <- eig_pos / sum(eig_pos)
dim1_pct <- round(100 * var_exp[1], 2)
dim2_pct <- round(100 * var_exp[2], 2)

plot_df <- df_sub %>%
  mutate(sample = rownames(df_sub)) %>%
  left_join(coords, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(
    fill_key = ifelse(kind == "SD", "SD", paste0("SI-", as.character(year_chr))),
    fill_key = factor(fill_key, levels = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)))
  )

# 6) PERMANOVA and multivariate dispersion (SD vs SI) 
meta_test <- plot_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, group2) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("sample")

# Ensure that metadata order matches the distance matrix
meta_test <- meta_test[rownames(as.matrix(dist_bc)), , drop = FALSE]

# PERMANOVA
adon <- vegan::adonis2(
  dist_bc ~ group2,
  data = meta_test,
  permutations = 999
)

adon_p  <- adon$`Pr(>F)`[1]
adon_r2 <- adon$R2[1]

# Homogeneity of multivariate dispersion
dispersion <- vegan::betadisper(
  dist_bc,
  group = factor(meta_test$group2)
)

dispersion_test <- vegan::permutest(
  dispersion,
  permutations = 999
)

dispersion_p <- dispersion_test$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]

# Annotation
anno_text <- paste0(
  "PERMANOVA\n",
  "P = ", format.pval(adon_p, digits = 3, eps = 0.001), "\n",
  "R\u00B2 = ", sprintf("%.4f", adon_r2), "\n",
  "Dispersion P = ",
  format.pval(dispersion_p, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
)

anno_text


aggregate(
  dispersion$distances,
  by = list(Group = dispersion$group),
  FUN = mean
)

# annotation placement (bottom-right)
x_rng <- range(plot_df$Dim1, na.rm = TRUE)
y_rng <- range(plot_df$Dim2, na.rm = TRUE)
anno_x <- x_rng[2] - 0.02 * diff(x_rng)
anno_y <- y_rng[1] + 0.02 * diff(y_rng)

# 7) Colors 
# SD: brown；SI: 5-step green gradient (light->dark)
si_cols <- colorRampPalette(c("#dce775", "#33691e"))(length(target_years))
names(si_cols) <- paste0("SI-", target_years)

fill_cols <- c("SD" = "#ff9800", si_cols)



# ellipse colors（SD vs SI ）
ellipse_line_cols <- c("SD" = "#e65100", "SI" = "#1b5e20")  
ellipse_fill_cols <- c("SD" = "#ffcc80", "SI" = "#e6ee9c")  

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Dim1, y = Dim2)) +
  # points
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = fill_key),
    shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 0.6,
    size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  
  # filled ellipse (under) 
stat_ellipse(
  aes(group = group2, fill = group2),
  type = "t", level = 0.95,
  geom = "polygon",
  alpha = 0.18,          
  color = NA,            
  show.legend = FALSE
) +
  
  # outline ellipse (over) 
stat_ellipse(
  aes(group = group2, color = group2),
  type = "t", level = 0.95,
  geom = "path",
  linewidth = 0.8,       
  show.legend = FALSE
) +
  
  # scale for points
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_cols,
    breaks = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    labels = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    name = "Group"
  ) +
  
  # scale for ellipse fill (SD/SI)
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(fill_cols, ellipse_fill_cols),
    breaks = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    labels = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    name = "Group"
  ) +
  
  # ellipse outline color
  scale_color_manual(values = ellipse_line_cols) +
  
  labs(
    x = paste0("Dim1 (", dim1_pct, "%)"),
    y = paste0("Dim2 (", dim2_pct, "%)")
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12,colour = "black"),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 12,colour = 'black')
  )
```

## 2.4 Automatic labeling difference with a b c
```{r using_alpha_diversity_as_an_example}
#Construct a function to calculate the median for each group, perform Kruskal-Wallis and Behrens-Fisher tests to obtain significance, and manually determine the "abc" levels based on the median values and p-values.
 library(mvtnorm)
 library(reshape2)
 # library(npmc)
 library(ggplot2)

"npmc" <-
   function(dataset, control=NULL, df=2, alpha=0.05){
     mvtnorm <- require(mvtnorm, quietly=TRUE);
     if (!mvtnorm)
     {
       msg <- paste("npmc requires the mvtnorm-package to calculate",
                    "p-values for the test-statistics. This package is not",
                    "available on your system, so these values and the",
                    "confidence-limits will be missing values in the output!\n",
                    sep="\n");
       warning(msg);
     }
     
     if (any(df==0:2)) 
       dfm <- c(3,2,1)[df+1]
     else
     {
       warning("Wrong value for df\nUsing Satterthwaite t-approximation\n");
       dfm <- 1;
     }
     
     if (alpha<=0 || alpha>=1)
       stop("alpha must be a value between 0 and 1");
     
     
     name <- attr(dataset, "name");
     desc <- attr(dataset, "description");
     
     
     ## Function definitions 
     
     
    
     ## ssq:
     ## Calculates a vector's sum of squares
     
     ssq <- function(x) sum(x*x);
     
     ##
     ## force.ps: 
     ## Forces a matrix to be positive semidefinite by replacing 
     ## all negative eigenvalues by zero.
     ## 
     force.ps <- function(M.in)
     {
       eig <- eigen(M.in, symmetric=TRUE);
       spec <- eig$values;
       if (adjusted <- any(spec<0))
       {
         spec[spec<0] <- 0;
         M <- eig$vectors %*% diag(spec) %*% t(eig$vectors);
         ginv <- diag(1/sqrt(diag(M)));
         M.out <- ginv %*% M %*% ginv;
         ##if ((msg <- all.equal(M.in,M.out))!=TRUE) attr(M.out, "msg") <- msg;
       }
       else
       {
         M.out <- M.in;
       }
       attr(M.out,"adjusted") <- adjusted; 
       return (M.out);
     }
     
     
     ##
     ## z.dist:
     ## Calculates the p-values for the teststatistics using the mvtnorm-package.
     ## The 'sides' parameter determines whether the p-values for the one-
     ## or two-sided test are calculated.
     ## The statistic is supposed to follow a multivariate t-statistic with
     ## correlation-matrix 'corr' and 'df' degrees of freedom. If df=0, the
     ## multivariate normal-distribution is used.
     ## We use the mvtnorm-package by Frank Bretz (www.bioinf.uni-hannover.de) 
     ## to calculate the corresponding p-values. These algorithms originally 
     ## calculate the value P(X<=stat) for the mentioned multivariate distributions, 
     ## i.e. the 1-sided p-value. In order to gain the 2-sided p-value as well, 
     ## we used the algorithms on the absolute value of the teststatistic in 
     ## combination with the inflated correlation-matrix
     ##   kronecker(matrix(c(1,-1,-1,1),ncol=2), corr)
     ##
     z.dist <- function(stat, corr, df=0, sides=2)
     {
       if (!mvtnorm) return (NA);
       
       if (sides==2)
       {
         corr <- kronecker(matrix(c(1,-1,-1,1),ncol=2), corr);
         stat <- abs(stat);
       }
       n <- ncol(corr);
       sapply(stat, function(arg) 
       {
         pmvt(
           lower=rep(-Inf, n), 
           upper=rep(arg, n), 
           df=as.integer(df), 
           corr=corr, 
           delta=rep(0,n)
         )[1];
       });     
     } 
     
     
     ##
     ## z.quantile:
     ## Calculates the corresponding quantiles of z.dist p-values
     ## (used for the confidence-intervals)
     ##
     z.quantile <- function(p=0.95, start=0, corr, df=0, sides=2)
     {
       if (!mvtnorm) return (NA);
       
       if (z.dist(start,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides) < p)
       {
         lower <- start;
         upper <- lower+1;
         while(z.dist(upper,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides) < p)
           upper <- upper+1;
       }
       else
       {
         upper <- start;
         lower <- upper-1;
         while(z.dist(lower,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides) > p)
           lower <- lower-1;
       }
       ur <- uniroot(f=function(arg) p-z.dist(arg,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides),
                     upper=upper, lower=lower
       );
       ur$root;
     }
     
     
     ## Calculations 
     
     ## sort the dataset by factor
     dataset$class <- factor(dataset$class);
     datord <- order(dataset$class);
     attrs <- attributes(dataset);
     dataset <- data.frame(lapply(dataset, "[", datord));
     attributes(dataset) <- attrs;
     
     ## general data characteristics
     #attach(dataset);
     fl <- levels(dataset$class);             # factor-levels
     a <- nlevels(dataset$class);             # number of factor-levels
     samples <- base::split(dataset$var, dataset$class);    # split the data in separate sample-vectors
     n <- sapply(samples, length);    # sample sizes
     #detach(dataset);
     
     if (is.null(control))
     {
       ## create indexing vectors for the all-pairs situation
       tmp <- expand.grid(1:a, 1:a);
       ind <- tmp[[1]] > tmp[[2]];
       vi <- tmp[[2]][ind];
       vj <- tmp[[1]][ind];
     }
     else
     {
       ## create indexing vectors for the many-to-one situation
       if (!any(fl==control))
       {
         msg <- paste("Wrong control-group specification\n",
                      "The data does not contain a group with factor-level ",
                      control,
                      sep="");
         stop(msg, FALSE);
       }
       cg <- which(fl==control);
       vi <- which((1:a)!=cg);
       vj <- rep(cg, a-1);
     }
     
     ## number of comparisons ( a*(a-1)/2 for all-pairs, (a-1) for many-to-one )
     nc <- length(vi);              
     
     ## labels describing the compared groups 
     cmpid <- paste(vi, "-", vj, sep="");
     
     ## pairwise pooled sample-sizes
     gn <- n[vi]+n[vj];
     
     ## internal rankings
     intRanks <- lapply(samples, rank);
     
     ## pairwise rankings
     pairRanks <- lapply(1:nc, function(arg) 
     {
       rank(c(samples[[vi[arg]]], samples[[vj[arg]]]));  
     });
     
     ## estimators for the relative effects
     pd <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg)
     {
       i <- vi[arg]; 
       j <- vj[arg];
       (sum(pairRanks[[arg]][(n[i]+1):gn[arg]])/n[j]-(n[j]+1)/2)/n[i];  
     });
     
     ## Calculations for the BF-test 
     ##
     dij <- dji <- list(0);
     
     sqij <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg) 
     {
       i <- vi[arg]; 
       j <- vj[arg];
       pr <- pairRanks[[arg]][(n[i]+1):gn[arg]];
       dij[[arg]] <<- pr - sum(pr)/n[j] - intRanks[[j]] + (n[j]+1)/2;
       ssq(dij[[arg]])/(n[i]*n[i]*(n[j]-1));
     });
     
     sqji <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg)
     {
       i <- vi[arg];  
       j <- vj[arg];
       pr <- pairRanks[[arg]][1:n[i]];
       dji[[arg]] <<- pr - sum(pr)/n[i] - intRanks[[i]] + (n[i]+1)/2;
       ssq(dji[[arg]])/(n[j]*n[j]*(n[i]-1));
     });
     
     ## diagonal elements of the covariance-matrix
     vd.bf <- gn*(sqij/n[vj] + sqji/n[vi]);
     
     ## mark and correct zero variances for further calculations
     singular.bf <- (vd.bf==0);
     vd.bf[singular.bf] <- 0.00000001;
     
     ## standard-deviation
     std.bf <- sqrt(vd.bf/gn);
     
     ## teststatistic
     t.bf <- (pd-0.5)*sqrt(gn/vd.bf);
     
     ## Satterthwaite approxiamtion for the degrees of freedom
     df.sw <- (n[vi]*sqij + n[vj]*sqji)^2 / 
       ((n[vi]*sqij)^2/(n[vj]-1) + (n[vj]*sqji)^2/(n[vi]-1));
     df.sw[is.nan(df.sw)] <- Inf;
     
     ## choose degrees of freedom 
     df <- if (dfm<3) max(1, if (dfm==2) min(gn-2) else min(df.sw)) else 0;
     
     
     ## Calculations for the Steel-test 
     ##
     ## the Steel-type correlation factors
     lambda <- sqrt(n[vi]/(gn+1));
     
     ## diagonal elements of the covariance-matrix
     vd.st <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg) ssq(pairRanks[[arg]]-(gn[arg]+1)/2)) / 
       (n[vi]*n[vj]*(gn-1));
     
     ## mark and correct zero variances for further calculations
     singular.st <- (vd.st==0);
     vd.st[singular.st] <- 0.00000001;
     
     ## standard-deviation
     std.st <- sqrt(vd.st/gn);
     
     ## teststatistic
     t.st <- (pd-0.5)*sqrt(gn/vd.st);
     
     
     ## Calculate the correlation-matrices (for both, BF and Steel) 
     ##    
     rho.bf <- rho.st <- diag(nc);
     for (x in 1:(nc-1))
     {
       for (y in (x+1):nc)
       {
         i <- vi[x]; j <- vj[x];
         v <- vi[y]; w <- vj[y];
         p <- c(i==v, j==w, i==w, j==v);
         if (sum(p)==1) 
         {      
           cl <- list(
             function()  (t(dji[[x]]) %*% dji[[y]]) / (n[j]*n[w]*n[i]*(n[i]-1)),
             function()  (t(dij[[x]]) %*% dij[[y]]) / (n[i]*n[v]*n[j]*(n[j]-1)),
             function() -(t(dji[[x]]) %*% dij[[y]]) / (n[i]*n[w]*n[i]*(n[i]-1)),
             function() -(t(dij[[x]]) %*% dji[[y]]) / (n[j]*n[v]*n[j]*(n[j]-1))
           );
           case <- (1:4)[p];
           rho.bf[x,y] <- rho.bf[y,x] <- 
             sqrt(gn[x]*gn[y]) / sqrt(vd.bf[x]*vd.bf[y]) * cl[[case]]()
           ;
           rho.st[x,y] <- rho.st[y,x] <- 
             {if (case>2) -1 else 1}*lambda[x]*lambda[y]
           ;
         }
       }
     }
     rho.bf <- force.ps(rho.bf);
     rho.st <- force.ps(rho.st);
     
     
     ## Calculate the p-values     (BF and Steel) 
     ##
     p1s.bf <- 1 - z.dist(t.bf, corr=rho.bf, df=df, sides=1);
     p2s.bf <- 1 - z.dist(t.bf, corr=rho.bf, df=df, sides=2);
     
     p1s.st <- 1 - z.dist(t.st, corr=rho.st, sides=1);
     p2s.st <- 1 - z.dist(t.st, corr=rho.st, sides=2);
     
     
     ## Calculate the confidence-limits (BF and Steel) 
     ##
     z.bf <- z.quantile(1-alpha, corr=rho.bf, df=df, sides=2);
     lcl.bf <- pd - std.bf*z.bf;
     ucl.bf <- pd + std.bf*z.bf;
     
     z.st <- z.quantile(1-alpha, corr=rho.st, sides=2);
     lcl.st <- pd - std.st*z.st;
     ucl.st <- pd + std.st*z.st;
     
     
     ## Output 
     
     ## Create the result-datastructures 
     ##    
     dataStructure <- data.frame("group index"=1:a, 
                                 "class level"=fl, 
                                 "nobs"=n
     );
     
     test.bf <- data.frame("cmp"=cmpid, 
                           "gn"=gn, 
                           "effect"=pd,
                           "lower.cl"=lcl.bf,
                           "upper.cl"=ucl.bf,
                           "variance"=vd.bf, 
                           "std"=std.bf, 
                           "statistic"=t.bf, 
                           "p-value 1s"=p1s.bf, 
                           "p-value 2s"=p2s.bf, 
                           "zero"=singular.bf
     ); 
     
     test.st <- data.frame("cmp"=cmpid, 
                           "gn"=gn, 
                           "effect"=pd, 
                           "lower.cl"=lcl.st,
                           "upper.cl"=ucl.st,
                           "variance"=vd.st, 
                           "std"=std.st, 
                           "statistic"=t.st, 
                           "p-value 1s"=p1s.st, 
                           "p-value 2s"=p2s.st, 
                           "zero"=singular.st
     ); 
     
     result <- list("data"=dataset,
                    "info"=dataStructure, 
                    "corr"=list("BF"=rho.bf, "Steel"=rho.st),
                    "test"=list("BF"=test.bf, "Steel"=test.st),
                    "control"=control,
                    "df.method"=dfm,
                    "df"=df,
                    "alpha"=alpha
     );
     
     class(result) <- "npmc";
     
     return (result);
     
   }
 

 
 ### with trend line 
 krus_BF <- function(data, groups, values, p = 0.05) {
   stat_kruskal <- NULL
   stat_BF <- NULL
   abc_list <- NULL
   
   #统计检验
   for (i in groups) {
     for (j in values) {
       
       #Kruskal-Wallis 检验，整体差异
       dat <- data[c(i, j)]
       names(dat) <- c('class', 'var')
       dat$class <- factor(dat$class)
       fit <- kruskal.test(var~class, dat)
       p_value <- fit$p.value
       
       #获取 Kruskal-Wallis 检验 p 值
       if (p_value < 0.001) sig <- '***'
       else if (p_value >= 0.001 & p_value < 0.01) sig <- '**'
       else if (p_value >= 0.01 & p_value < 0.05) sig <- '*'
       else sig <- ''
       stat_kruskal <- rbind(stat_kruskal, c(paste(i, j, sep = '/'), p_value, sig))
       
       #Behrens-Fisher 检验（npmc 包），非参数多重比较
       BF_test <- npmc(dataset = dat, control=NULL, df = 2, alpha = 0.05)
       BF <- BF_test$test$BF
       info <- BF_test$info
       
       BF$group <- paste(i, j, sep = '/')
       for (l in 1:nrow(BF)) {
         x <- strsplit(as.vector(BF[l,'cmp']), '-')[[1]]
         BF[l,'class1'] <- rownames(info)[which(info$group.index == x[1])]
         BF[l,'class2'] <- rownames(info)[which(info$group.index == x[2])]
       }
       stat_BF <- rbind(stat_BF, BF[c(12:14, 2:11)])
       
       #Behrens-Fisher 检验 p 值矩阵获取
       stat_p <- BF[c(13, 14, 10)]
       stat_p1 <- stat_p[c(2, 1, 3)]
       names(stat_p1)[1:2] <- c('class1', 'class2')
       stat_p <- rbind(stat_p, stat_p1)
       stat_p <- dcast(stat_p, class1~class2, value.var = 'p.value.2s')
       rownames(stat_p) <- stat_p$class1
       
       #计算各组中位数
       abc_ij <- aggregate(dat$var, by = list(dat$class), FUN = mean)
       abc_ij$group <- i
       abc_ij$var <- j
       abc_ij <- abc_ij[c(3, 4, 1, 2)]
       names(abc_ij) <- c('group', 'var', 'class', 'median')
       
       #根据中位数和 p 值，手动添加显著性标记“abc”
       abc_ij <- abc_ij[order(abc_ij$median, decreasing = TRUE), ]
       class <- as.vector(abc_ij$class)
       
       m = 1; n = 2; l = 1
       abc_ij[m,'sig'] <- letters[l]
       while (n < length(class)) {
         for (n in (m+1):length(class)) {
           if (stat_p[class[m],class[n]] < p) {
             abc_ij[n,'sig'] <- letters[l+1]
             if (n - m != 1) {
               for (x in (m+1):(n-1)) {
                 if (stat_p[class[x],class[n]] < p) abc_ij[x,'sig'] <- letters[l]
                 else abc_ij[x,'sig'] <- paste(letters[l], letters[l+1], sep = '')
               }
             }
             l = l + 1
             m = n
             break
           }
         }
       }
       abc_ij[(m:n),'sig'] <- letters[l]
       
       abc_list <- rbind(abc_list, abc_ij)
     }
   }
   
   #ggplot2 作图，箱线图
   data <- melt(data[c(groups, values)], id = groups)
   data <- melt(data, id = c('variable', 'value'))
   data <- data[c(3, 1, 4, 2)]
   names(data) <- c('group', 'var', 'class', 'value')
   
   data$type <- data$class
 # data['type'][data['type'] == 4 | data['type'] == 7 | data['type'] == 9] <- 'DI'
   data['type'][data['type'] == 11 | data['type'] == 12 | data['type'] == 14 | data['type'] == 15 | data['type'] == 17] <- 'SI'
   
   value_max <- aggregate(data$value, by = list(data$group, data$var), FUN = max)
   names(value_max) <- c('group', 'var', 'value')
   value_max <- merge(value_max, abc_list[-4], by = c('group', 'var'))
   
   
   #cgf
  # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#bcbddc","#9e9ac8","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") #si
   
   #data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","OsF","IsF","4","7","9", "11","12","14","15","17"))
   #see
   # myPalette = c('#D9D9D9','#80B1D3','#FDB462','#B0DB67')
   #data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("Sd","Nbc","Bc","Nr"))
   
   # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") 
   
   # data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","4","7","9", "11","12","14","15","17"))
   
   #cgf without OSF and ISF
 # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") #si
   
  # data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","4","7","9", "11","12","14","15","17"))
   
   #cgf for sd and si
   myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") #si
   
   data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","11","12","14","15","17"))
   
   # cgf sd di
  # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43") #si
   
   #data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","4","7","9"))
   
   plot_box_g <- ggplot(data = data, aes(x = class, y = value, fill = class)) +
     scale_fill_manual(values = myPalette) +
     facet_grid(. ~ var) + facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y",ncol = 6) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(3.5,0.50,3.5,0.50,"cm"))) +
     geom_boxplot(aes(x=class, y=value,group=class),outlier.shape = NA) + 
     geom_beeswarm(color = "black", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7,dodge.width = 0.05) +
     geom_smooth(data = subset(data,type=='SI'), aes(group=1), method = "glm",color = "#225EA8", se=F,alpha = 0.8) +
     #geom_smooth(data = subset(data,type=='DI'), aes(group=1), method = "glm",color = "#B34300", se=F,alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = value_max, aes(label = sig, y = value + 0.05*value), size = 8) +
     theme_bw()+ ylab("") + xlab('') +
     theme(legend.position = "none",
           panel.grid=element_blank()) +
     theme(text=element_text(size = 25)) +
     theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill="#FFFFFF")) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 32)) 
   
   plot_box_m <- ggplot(data = data, aes(x = class, y = value, fill = class)) +
     scale_fill_manual(values = myPalette) +
     facet_grid(. ~ var) + facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y",ncol = 6) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(3.5,0.50,3.5,0.50,"cm"))) +
     geom_boxplot(aes(x=class, y=value,group=class)) + geom_beeswarm(color = "black", size = 0.2, alpha = 0.4,dodge.width = 0.05) +
     stat_summary(data = subset(data,type=='SI'),fun=median, geom="line", aes(group=1), color = "#225EA8", size=1) +
   #  stat_summary(data = subset(data,type=='DI'),fun=median, geom="line", aes(group=1), color = "#B34300", size=1) +
   #  geom_text(data = value_max, aes(label = sig, y = value + 0.05*value), size = 8) +
     theme_bw()+ ylab("") + xlab('') +
     theme(legend.position = "none",
           panel.grid=element_blank()) +
     theme(text=element_text(size = 25)) +
     theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill="#FFFFFF")) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 32)) 
   
   #return
   stat_kruskal <- data.frame(stat_kruskal, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   names(stat_kruskal) <- c('group', 'kruskal_pvalue', 'sig')
   stat_kruskal$kruskal_pvalue <- as.numeric(stat_kruskal$kruskal_pvalue)
   
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s < 0.001),'sig.2s'] <- '***'
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s >= 0.001 & stat_BF$p.value.2s < 0.01),'sig.2s'] <- '**'
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s >= 0.01 & stat_BF$p.value.2s < 0.05),'sig.2s'] <- '*'
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s >= 0.05),'sig.2s'] <- ''
   
   list(data = value_max, stat = list(kruskal = stat_kruskal, BF_p = stat_BF, BF_abc = abc_list), plot_g = plot_box_g, plot_m = plot_box_m)
 }
```

## 2.7 GLM regression model and visualization

```{r GLM}
# to detect valuables changed with ages, here is one of the example with figure 2C
library(pscl)
library(MASS)
data <- read.delim('~/Desktop/replot/c_means/species/si_species.txt',row.names = 1,
                   sep = '\t',stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
data <- data[1:217,]
data <- as.data.frame(apply(data,2,as.numeric))
View(data)
# Convert year to numeric (if necessary)
age <- as.numeric(data$year)

# Create a list of response variables
response_vars <- colnames(data)[2:76]

# Create an empty data frame to store the results
results <- data.frame(response_var = numeric(),
                      slope_coeff = numeric(),
                      p_value = numeric(),
                      adj_r_square = numeric(),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#family = quasipoisson(link = "log")  when not in normal distribution
# Loop over the response variables and fit a GLM for each
for (i in seq_along(response_vars)) {
  # Fit the GLM with Poisson error distribution and log link function
  model <- glm(data[, response_vars[i]] ~ age, data = data)
  # Check assumptions and extract slope coefficient and p-value for whole model
  
  #model <- glm(data[, response_vars[i]] ~ age, data = data)
 # norm_test <- shapiro.test(resid(model)) #to perform the Shapiro-Wilk normality test on a vector or a data frame column
 # print(norm_test)
  p_val <- summary(model)$coefficients[2,4]
  print(p_val)
  slope_coeff <- summary(model)$coefficients[2, 1]
  adj_r_square <- with(summary(model), 1 - deviance/null.deviance)
  
  # Adjust p-value using BH method
  #adj_p_val <- p.adjust(p_val, method = "BH")
  
  # Store the results in the data frame
  results[i, ] <- list(response_var = response_vars[i],
                       slope_coeff = slope_coeff,
                       p_value = p_val,
                       adj_r_square = adj_r_square)
  }

final_result <- cbind(results,padjust = p.adjust(results[,"p_value"], method="BH"))


table(final_result$padjust < 0.05)

#write.table(final_result, '/Users/chenqiong/Desktop/replot/metabo//si_species_glm.txt',sep="\t", col.names = NA,quote = FALSE)
```

## 2.9 AEM

```{r AEM}

    library(ade4)
    library(mvpart)
    library(vegan)
    library(AEM)
    # library(PCMN)
    library(packfor)

 weight.time <- function(dates, distmat=NULL,alpha=2, beta=NULL, max.d=NULL, unit.angle="degrees", rot.angle=0, rm.same.y=TRUE,   plot.connexions=TRUE){
      #
      # dates : vector of dates.
      # alpha : exponent of the first weighting function
      # beta  : exponent of the second weighting function
      # max.d : maximum distance for weighting. Default value (not recommended in most 
      #         cases): the maximum distance among dates in the 'dates' vector. 
      #         A more meaningful solution in many applications is to compute a  
      #         Moran's I correlogram (for univariate data) or a Mantel correlogram 
      #         (for multivariate data), and use the distance where the correlation 
      #         becomes 0 as the value for max.d.
      #
      ### F. Guillaume Blanchet - August 2013
      ##########################################################################################
      n  <- length(dates)
      nb <- cell2nb(1,n)
      xy <- cbind(1:n, rep(1, n), dates)
      w  <- weight.edges(nb.object=nb, coords=xy, distmat=distmat, alpha=alpha, beta=beta, max.d=max.d, unit.angle=unit.angle, rot.angle=rot.angle, rm.same.y=rm.same.y, plot.connexions=plot.connexions)	
      w
    }
```

# Create function to identify RMSE for best lambda, 
# where x = RMSE vector, y = lambda vector, &  z = optimal lambda value
RMSE_lasso <- function(x, y, z){
  temp <- data.frame(x, y)
  colnames(temp) <- c("RMSE", "lambda_val")
  rownum <- which(temp$lambda_val==z)
  print(temp[rownum,]$RMSE)
}

           y=model1$results$lambda,   # y = lambda vector
           z=model1$bestTune$lambda)  # z = optimal lambda value


# Create function to identify Rsquared for best lambda, 
# where x = Rsquared vector, y = lambda vector, &  z = optimal lambda value
Rsquared_lasso <- function(x, y, z){
  temp <- data.frame(x, y)
  colnames(temp) <- c("Rsquared", "lambda_val")
  rownum <- which(temp$lambda_val==z)
  print(temp[rownum,]$Rsquared)
}

concordance_index <- function(predictions, truth) {
  n <- length(predictions)
  n_pairs <- 0
  n_concordant <- 0
  
  for (i in 1:(n-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):n) {
      if (truth[i] != truth[j]) {
        n_pairs <- n_pairs + 1
        if ((predictions[i] < predictions[j] && truth[i] < truth[j]) || 
            (predictions[i] > predictions[j] && truth[i] > truth[j])) {
          n_concordant <- n_concordant + 1
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(n_concordant / n_pairs)
}


cvnested = function(data.frame, truth.frame, k){ #data.frame to train on, k is for outer fold
  print(ncol(data.frame))
  flds <- createFolds(1:ncol(data.frame), k = k, list = TRUE, returnTrain = FALSE)
  mse = c() # Mean Squared Error
  rmse = c() # Root Mean Squared Error
  mae = c() # Mean Absolute Error
  r_squared = c() # R-squared
  c_index = c() # Concordance Index
  predict.values.df = data.frame("carbon"=c())
  truth.values = c()
  
  for (i in 1:length(flds)){#outer
    test.outer = data.frame[, c(flds[[i]])]
    truth.test.outer = truth.frame$carbon[c(flds[[i]])]
    
    train.outer = data.frame[, -c(flds[[i]])]
    truth.train.outer = truth.frame$carbon[-c(flds[[i]])]
    
    cvglmfit = cv.glmnet(x = t(train.outer),
                         y = (truth.train.outer),
                         family = "gaussian")
    s0 = cvglmfit$lambda.1se
    
    glmfit = glmnet(x = t(train.outer),
                    y = (truth.train.outer),
                    family = "gaussian")
    
    pred = predict(glmfit, t(test.outer),
                   type = "response", s = s0)
    pred.values = predict(glmfit, t(test.outer),
                          type = "response", s = s0)
    pred.values.df = data.frame(pred.values)
    colnames(pred.values.df) = c("carbon")
    predict.values.df = rbind(predict.values.df, pred.values.df)
    
    mse = c(mse, mean((pred - truth.test.outer)^2)) # 计算 Mean Squared Error 并将其存储在 mse 向量中
    rmse = c(rmse, sqrt(mean((pred - truth.test.outer)^2))) # 计算 Root Mean Squared Error 并将其存储在 rmse 向量中
    mae = c(mae, mean(abs(pred - truth.test.outer))) # 计算 Mean Absolute Error 并将其存储在 mae 向量中
    r_squared = c(r_squared, 1 - sum((truth.test.outer - pred)^2) / sum((truth.test.outer - mean(truth.test.outer))^2)) # 计算 R-squared 并将其存储在 r_squared 向量中
    c_index = c(c_index, concordance_index(pred, truth.test.outer)) # 计算 Concordance Index 并将其存储在 c_index 向量中
  }#outer
  
  predict.values.df = predict.values.df[order(rownames(predict.values.df)),]
  
  cvglmfit.final = cv.glmnet(x = t(data.frame),
                             y = (truth.frame$carbon),
                             family = "gaussian")
  s0.model = cvglmfit.final$lambda.1se
  glmfit.final = glmnet(x = t(data.frame),
                        y = (truth.frame$carbon),
                        family = "gaussian")
  
  pred.all = predict(glmfit.final, t(data.frame), type = "response", s=s0.model)
  mse.all = mean((pred.all - truth.frame$carbon)^2) # 计算整个数据集的 Mean Squared Error
  rmse.all = sqrt(mean((pred.all - truth.frame$carbon)^2)) # 计算整个数据集的 Root Mean Squared Error
  mae.all = mean(abs(pred.all - truth.frame$carbon)) # 计算整个数据集的 Mean Absolute Error
  r_squared.all = 1 - sum((truth.frame$carbon - pred.all)^2) / sum((truth.frame$carbon - mean(truth.frame$carbon))^2) # 计算整个数据集的 R-squared
  c_index.all = concordance_index(pred.all, truth.frame$carbon) # 计算整个数据集的 Concordance Index
  
  print(mse.all)
  print(rmse.all)
  print(mae.all)
  print(r_squared.all)
  print(c_index.all)
  
  # 提取模型中最重要的 Top 20 个变量
  coefs = coef(glmfit.final, s = s0.model)
  coefs = coefs[-1, , drop = FALSE]  # 删除截距项
  coefs_abs = abs(coefs) # 取绝对值
  top_var_indices = order(coefs_abs, decreasing = TRUE)[1:20] # 获取 Top 20 个变量的索引
  top_var_names = rownames(coefs)[top_var_indices] # 获取 Top 20 个变量的名称
  imp_vars = coefs[top_var_indices, , drop = FALSE] # 提取最重要的 Top 20 个变量
  rownames(imp_vars) = top_var_names # 设置变量名称
  
  imp_vars_abs = coefs_abs[top_var_indices, , drop = FALSE] # 提取最重要的 Top 20 个变量的绝对值（重要性）
  rownames(imp_vars_abs) = top_var_names # 设置变量名称
  
  cat("Top 20 Important Variables and their Coefficients:\n")
  print(imp_vars)
  
  cat("Top 20 Important Variables and their Importance (Absolute Coefficients):\n")
  print(imp_vars_abs)
  
  return(list(mse = mse, rmse = rmse, mae = mae, r_squared = r_squared, c_index = c_index,
              predict.values = predict.values.df, imp_variable = as.matrix(imp_vars), imp_variable_coe = as.matrix(imp_vars_abs)))
}

#cvnest function, p is not used for glmnet predictions
# relabeled 11, 12, 14, 15yr as "spring", "summer", "fall","winter"
cvnested = function(data.frame, truth.frame, k, p){ #data.frame to train on, k is for outter fold, p is for inner fold
  print(ncol(data.frame))
  flds <- createFolds(1:ncol(data.frame), k = k, list = TRUE, returnTrain = FALSE)
  auc = c()
  predict.values.df = data.frame(spring=c(), summer=c(), fall=c(), winter=c())
  truth.values = c()
  #print(length(flds))
  for (i in 1:length(flds)){#outter
    test.outter = data.frame[, c(flds[[i]])]
    truth.test.outter = truth.frame$season[c(flds[[i]])]
    #print(truth.test.outter)
    #print(flds[[i]])
    train.outter = data.frame[, -c(flds[[i]])]
    truth.train.outter = truth.frame$season[-c(flds[[i]])]
    fraction = table(truth.train.outter)/length(truth.train.outter)
    weights = 1 - fraction[as.character(truth.train.outter)]
    #print(truth.train.outter)
    #print(dim(train.outter))
    #cv.glmnet takes care of inner loop training
    cvglmfit = cv.glmnet(x = t(train.outter),
                         y = factor(truth.train.outter),
                         family = "multinomial", weights = weights)
    s0 = cvglmfit$lambda.1se
    #hyper-parameter
    #fit train dataset with given hyper-parameter
    glmfit = glmnet(x = t(train.outter),
                    y = factor(truth.train.outter),
                    family = "multinomial")
    #predict on testing dataset
    pred = predict(glmfit, t(test.outter),
                   type = "class", s = s0)
    pred.values = predict(glmfit, t(test.outter),
                          type = "response", s = s0)
    pred.values.df = data.frame(pred.values)
    colnames(pred.values.df) = c("spring", "summer", "fall","winter")
    predict.values.df = rbind(predict.values.df, pred.values.df)
    
    truth.values=c(truth.values, truth.test.outter)
    confusion_table = table(predicted = pred, truth = factor(truth.test.outter))
    #print(confusion_table)
    mROC = multiclass.roc(as.numeric(factor(truth.test.outter)), as.numeric(factor(pred[,1])))
    #print(auc(mROC))
    auc = c(auc, mROC$auc)
    #test model selected by inner to the outter test set
  }#outter
  #print(dim(predict.values.df))
  #print(rownames(predict.values.df))
  #print(truth.values) #this is not necessary as the truth remains to be the truth
  #reodering the dataframe to be consistent between resamplings.
  predict.values.df = predict.values.df[order(rownames(predict.values.df)),]
  
  #fit build model on whole dataset and testing on external dataset
  fraction = table(truth.frame$season)/length(truth.frame$season)
  weights = 1 - fraction[as.character(truth.frame$season)]
  cvglmfit.final = cv.glmnet(x = t(data.frame),
                             y = factor(truth.frame$season),
                             family = "multinomial", weights = weights)
  s0.model = cvglmfit.final$lambda.1se
  glmfit.final = glmnet(x = t(data.frame),
                        y = factor(truth.frame$season),
                        family = "multinomial")
  #use on external dataset
  # print(paste0("the s0 used is ", s0.model))
  pred.all = predict(glmfit.final, t(data.frame), type = "class", s=s0.model)
  confusion_table.all = table(predicted = factor(pred.all, levels=c("spring", "summer", "fall","winter")), truth = factor(truth.frame$season))
  print(confusion_table.all)
  metrics = check.model.performance(factor(pred.all, levels=c("spring", "summer", "fall","winter")),factor(truth.frame$season))
  #print(metrics)
  mROC.all = multiclass.roc(as.numeric(factor(truth.frame$season)), as.numeric(factor(pred.all[,1])))
  print(mROC.all$auc)
  return(list(auc = auc, metrics=metrics, predict.values=predict.values.df))
}
